market.title: EU Instant Payments Mandate: CEE Banks Face Implementation Hurdles
market.summary_short: The EU's Instant Payments Regulation is nearing critical implementation phases, posing significant challenges for banks, particularly in the CEE region, to ensure 24/7/365 processing capabilities and fee parity. Corporates must prepare for faster liquidity management and fraud detection.
market.summary_detail: The European Union's Instant Payments Regulation mandates that all euro credit transfers be processed instantly, 24/7/365, with no additional fees compared to standard SEPA credit transfers. The first key deadline for receiving instant payments is January 2025, with sending capabilities required by January 2026 for Eurozone countries, and later for non-Eurozone members. CEE banks, many operating in non-Eurozone countries but handling EUR payments, face complex technical upgrades to their core banking systems and liquidity management frameworks. The regulation also includes a Verification of Payee (VoP) requirement to combat fraud, which banks must integrate into their instant payment offerings. This shift necessitates significant investment in infrastructure and operational adjustments for both financial institutions and their corporate clients.
key_points: Mandatory instant processing for EUR credit transfers.
24/7/365 availability and no extra fees.
VoP requirement to enhance fraud prevention.
Key deadlines: Jan 2025 (receive), Jan 2026 (send for Eurozone).
market.rbi_cash_management: This regulation is critical for RBI CMIplus as it directly impacts payment processing in all CEE markets. CMIplus must ensure full compliance with instant payment capabilities, VoP integration, and competitive fee structures across its network banks, supporting both Eurozone and non-Eurozone CEE countries.

market.title: PSD3 Proposals Target Enhanced Open Banking, Fraud Prevention
market.summary_short: The European Commission's proposed PSD3 and Payment Services Regulation (PSR) aim to strengthen open banking frameworks, improve consumer protection, and significantly bolster fraud prevention measures across the EU. These legislative changes will redefine the landscape for payment service providers and corporate treasuries.
market.summary_detail: The new legislative package, comprising PSD3 and the PSR, seeks to replace PSD2 with updated rules addressing gaps and new challenges in the digital payment ecosystem. Key proposals include making open banking data sharing more robust and secure, enhancing user control over their financial data, and mandating stronger fraud prevention tools, particularly for instant payments and spoofing scams. For corporates, this means potential for more sophisticated API-driven treasury solutions, but also increased compliance burdens related to security and data protection. The regulation is expected to streamline payment operations while placing greater responsibility on banks and payment service providers to protect users from financial crime.

Focus on stronger fraud prevention, especially for instant payments.
Improved consumer data control and security.
Impacts API-driven treasury solutions and compliance.
market.rbi_cash_management: PSD3 and PSR are highly relevant for CMIplus as they will shape future API offerings, fraud prevention strategies, and overall compliance requirements for payment services in CEE. RBI must proactively adapt its platform and services to meet new regulatory standards and leverage enhanced open banking capabilities.

market.title: AI Revolutionizes Payment Fraud Detection for Corporates
market.summary_short: Financial institutions and corporates are increasingly deploying Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) solutions to combat sophisticated payment fraud, especially with the rise of instant payments. These technologies offer real-time anomaly detection and predictive analytics, significantly enhancing security.
market.summary_detail: The rapid adoption of instant payments has brought increased efficiency but also new challenges in fraud prevention, as fraudulent transactions must be identified and blocked within seconds. AI and ML algorithms are proving instrumental in this fight, capable of analyzing vast datasets of transaction patterns, user behavior, and network anomalies in real-time. These systems can detect deviations that human analysts or rule-based systems might miss, such as unusual payment amounts, recipient changes, or atypical geographic locations. Corporates are integrating AI-powered tools into their treasury systems to protect against Business Email Compromise (BEC), invoice fraud, and account takeover attempts, working closely with their banking partners to leverage these advanced capabilities.

Analyzes transaction patterns, user behavior, and network anomalies.
Detects sophisticated fraud like BEC and account takeovers.
Requires collaboration between corporates and banks.

market.title: PSD3: EU Commission Proposes New Payment Services Directive
market.summary_short: The European Commission has unveiled its proposal for the third Payment Services Directive (PSD3), aiming to enhance payment security and foster innovation. Key changes include strengthening fraud prevention measures and promoting Open Banking.
market.summary_detail: The proposed PSD3 aims to modernize the regulatory framework for payment services across the EU, building on the successes and lessons learned from PSD2. A significant focus is placed on combating payment fraud through enhanced data sharing and stronger authentication protocols. The directive also seeks to further unlock the potential of Open Banking by clarifying API access rules and encouraging greater competition among payment service providers. This evolution is expected to drive the development of new payment solutions and improve the overall customer experience. The legislative process will now involve the European Parliament and Council for adoption, with potential implementation timelines to be determined.

regulatory.title: EU Instant Payments Regulation: Mandatory Offering and Receipt
regulatory.summary_short: The ECB is overseeing the implementation of the new EU Instant Payments Regulation, requiring banks to offer and receive instant credit transfers in euro. This regulation aims to make instant payments universally available and affordable across the EU and EEA.
regulatory.summary_detail: The EU Instant Payments Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2024/886) mandates Payment Service Providers (PSPs) in the EU/EEA to offer instant credit transfers in euro at the same or lower cost as standard credit transfers. PSPs must be able to receive instant payments by early 2025 and send them by early 2026. The ECB, in its oversight role, ensures smooth adoption and compliance, promoting real-time payment processing and liquidity management. This regulation significantly impacts retail and corporate payments, driving faster settlement and improved cash flow for businesses, and includes a Verification of Payee (VoP) requirement.
key_points: Mandatory receipt of instant payments by early 2025.
Mandatory offering of instant payments by early 2026.
Pricing must be equal to or lower than standard credit transfers.
Verification of Payee (VoP) service required to mitigate fraud.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: CMIplus must ensure full compliance with the Instant Payments Regulation, enabling both sending and receiving instant SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT Inst) for corporate clients. This includes integrating VoP services and adapting pricing models to meet the 'no higher cost' requirement.

regulatory.title: Continuous Evolution and Oversight of SEPA Payment Schemes
regulatory.summary_short: The ECB maintains continuous oversight of SEPA schemes (SCT, SDD, SCT Inst), ensuring their smooth functioning, security, and adaptation to market needs. Regular updates to SEPA rulebooks and technical standards are part of this ongoing process.
regulatory.summary_detail: SEPA remains the cornerstone of euro retail payments, and the ECB actively participates in its governance and oversight through the Eurosystem. This involves monitoring compliance with SEPA rules, facilitating market dialogue, and contributing to the evolution of the SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT), SEPA Direct Debit (SDD), and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) schemes. Banks must continuously adapt their systems and processes to comply with updated SEPA rulebooks, which incorporate changes related to fraud prevention, operational efficiency, and new technologies. This ensures harmonized and secure payment processing across the euro area.
key_points: Adherence to updated SEPA Rulebooks for SCT, SDD, SCT Inst.
Continuous monitoring of SEPA scheme compliance by PSPs.
Participation in market dialogue for future SEPA developments.
Implementation of enhanced fraud prevention measures within SEPA.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: CMIplus must ensure its SEPA processing capabilities are always aligned with the latest SEPA Rulebook versions and technical standards. This includes adapting to any new requirements for SCT, SDD, and SCT Inst, particularly regarding data formats (ISO 20022) and operational procedures.

regulatory.summary_detail: Following the successful T2-T2S consolidation and migration to ISO 20022, the ECB's TARGET Services continue to evolve. T2 (the new RTGS system) and TIPS (TARGET Instant Payment Settlement) are critical components of the European financial market infrastructure. The ongoing work includes monitoring the stability and performance of these systems, addressing any post-migration adaptations, and exploring future enhancements. Banks must ensure their internal systems and connectivity remain fully compatible with the ISO 20022 messaging standards used by TARGET Services, which impacts all high-value and instant payments settled through the Eurosystem.
key_points: Continued adherence to ISO 20022 standards for T2 and TIPS.
Monitoring and adaptation to post-migration enhancements in TARGET Services.
Ensuring robust connectivity and operational resilience with Eurosystem infrastructure.
Participation in market contact groups for future TARGET developments.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: CMIplus, as a platform for international corporates, relies on seamless integration with TARGET Services. RBI must ensure its systems are fully compliant with ISO 20022 for all relevant payment types processed via T2 and TIPS, and stay updated on any future technical or operational changes to maintain efficient liquidity management.

regulatory.title: EU regulatory developments impact liquidity management, report highlights
regulatory.summary_short: New EBA report details how Instant Payments Regulation, PSR, and PSD3 will transform liquidity management. These measures aim to boost instant payments and create a level playing field.
regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) has published a report by its Liquidity Management Working Group (LMWG) on the significant impact of upcoming EU regulatory developments on liquidity management. The report specifically examines the Instant Payments Regulation (IPR), the proposed Payment Services Regulation (PSR), and the forthcoming Payment Services Directive 3 (PSD3). These initiatives are expected to drive increased adoption of instant payments, foster greater competition among market participants, and fundamentally alter how financial institutions manage their liquidity. The LMWG paper provides insights into the expected changes and their implications for the financial sector.
key_points: Instant Payments Regulation (IPR) to accelerate uptake of instant payments.
Proposed Payment Services Regulation (PSR) and PSD3 to reshape the regulatory landscape.

regulatory.title: FIDA regulation: opportunities and challenges for open data economy
regulatory.summary_short: EBA survey reveals expert views on the proposed Financial Data Access (FIDA) regulation. The report offers recommendations for market participants preparing for implementation.
regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) has released a report detailing the findings of a survey on the proposed Financial Data Access (FIDA) regulation. The survey gathered insights from financial institution experts across more than 15 European countries, focusing on the potential opportunities and challenges presented by FIDA. The report aims to provide a practitioner's perspective on how this regulation could act as a catalyst for an open data economy. It includes practical recommendations and frameworks designed to assist market participants in their preparation for FIDA implementation.
key_points: Survey of financial institution experts across 15+ European countries.
Focus on opportunities and challenges of the proposed FIDA regulation.
Report provides practical recommendations and frameworks for implementation.
Aims to foster an open data economy in the financial sector.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: CMIplus should analyze the implications of the FIDA regulation for corporate treasury and data access. Understanding the new data sharing requirements and potential benefits will be important for advising CEE corporates on leveraging open finance opportunities.
